document_title: Royal Bank of Canada Annual Report 2025
section: Management's Discussion and Analysis — Credit risk — Credit risk limits
excerpt: Concentration risk is defined as the risk arising from an overexposure in particular industry sectors, countries, or credit products within the portfolio, reflecting the potential for credit deterioration and default to be relatively highly correlated.
interpretation: OUR INTERPRETATION (not issuer text): Framework, not oil-specific: RBC treats industry-sector overexposure as a correlated-default risk. It is the lens for reading the oil-and-gas rows in Tables 41 and 72-74.

document_title: Royal Bank of Canada Annual Report 2025
section: Management's Discussion and Analysis — Credit risk exposure by portfolio, sector and geography (Table 41)
interpretation: OUR INTERPRETATION (not issuer text): Disclosed fact: oil-and-gas EAD of $18,880 million at October 31, 2025 (2024: $19,107 million). Our arithmetic, not RBC's: about 0.83% of total EAD ($2,272,558 million) and 1.34% of total wholesale EAD. Almost half (8,671) is undrawn commitments, which could be drawn under stress.

document_title: Royal Bank of Canada Annual Report 2025
section: Management's Discussion and Analysis — Supplementary information — Loans and acceptances by portfolio and sector (Table 72)
interpretation: OUR INTERPRETATION (not issuer text): Disclosed fact: drawn oil-and-gas loans and acceptances of $6,352 million (2024: $6,362 million). Our arithmetic: about 0.61% of total loans and acceptances and 1.6% of wholesale loans. Flat year over year while total loans grew about 6%.

document_title: Royal Bank of Canada Annual Report 2025
section: Note 2 Summary of material accounting policies, estimates and judgments — Allowance for credit losses — Use of forward-looking information
excerpt: Macroeconomic variables used in our expected credit loss models include, but are not limited to, unemployment rates, gross domestic product growth rates, equity return indices, commodity prices and Canadian housing prices.
interpretation: OUR INTERPRETATION (not issuer text): Mechanism: commodity prices are an input to RBC's expected-credit-loss models, so an oil price shock can change allowances through forward-looking scenarios. RBC does not say how large that effect is or which commodities are used.

document_title: Royal Bank of Canada Annual Report 2025
section: Note 5 Loans and allowance for credit losses — Key inputs and assumptions — Scenario design and weightings
excerpt: During Q2 2025, in response to U.S. international trade policy, we designed a trade disruption scenario to replace our energy sector scenario.
interpretation: OUR INTERPRETATION (not issuer text): Disclosed fact: RBC had an energy-sector downside scenario and replaced it in Q2 2025. Our reading: management judged trade disruption a more relevant downside than an energy shock for fiscal 2025 allowances. This is not evidence that energy risk disappeared.
